protractor_read.name: Measure With a Protractor (option)
protractor_read.teaches: measuring angles in whole degrees with a protractor: which scale, from 0
protractor_read.representation: write the angle in degrees — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form
protractor_read.why: measure_angles is MC choice of 4 degree values

points_lines_rays.name: Point, Line, Segment or Ray?
points_lines_rays.teaches: identifying and drawing points, lines, line segments, rays, right/acute/obtuse angles and perpendicular and parallel lines, and finding them in 2-D figures
points_lines_rays.representation: write the word from a bank; draw on the grid (the key shows one drawing) — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form

map.taskType: select the figure: line, ray, segment

make_line_plot.name: Make a Line Plot
make_line_plot.teaches: measuring objects (ruler pictures) or reading a data list, then making a line plot (dot plot) on a scale of whole numbers, halves, quarters or eighths, and solving problems from it
make_line_plot.representation: draw the × marks; write the answers — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form

map.taskType: build a line plot from data (drag Xs)

bar_graph_scale.option: scale 2, 5 or 10 per square (draw a scaled bar graph)
bar_graph_scale.name: Draw a Scaled Bar Graph (option)
bar_graph_scale.teaches: drawing scaled bar graphs and answering one- and two-step "how many more / less" questions from them
bar_graph_scale.representation: draw the bars; write the answer — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form

pictogram_scale.name: Pictograms with a Key (option)
pictogram_scale.teaches: drawing pictograms where one picture stands for 2, 5 or 10, including half pictures

map.taskType: build/read a picture graph with a key

compare_lengths.name: Compare Lengths
compare_lengths.teaches: comparing and ordering lengths in mixed units (1 m 20 cm vs 125 cm)
compare_lengths.representation: two labelled bars; write <, > or = after converting

map.taskType: compare two lengths; how much longer

compare_lengths.why: order_objects_length orders only; no "how much longer"

ruler_difference.option: task "how much longer?": two objects on one ruler; cm and inches
ruler_difference.name: How Much Longer? (option)
ruler_difference.teaches: measuring two objects with a standard unit and finding how much longer one is
ruler_difference.representation: write both lengths and the difference with the unit — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form

map.taskType: two objects on one ruler, difference

missing_lengths.name: Missing Lengths in Rectilinear Shapes
missing_lengths.teaches: finding missing side lengths in rectilinear shapes and then their perimeter
missing_lengths.representation: an L or T shape with some sides labelled; write the missing lengths

map.taskType: missing side of a rectilinear shape

missing_lengths.why: perimeter gives one missing-side item per ~3 for rectangles only

same_area.name: Same Area, Different Perimeter
same_area.teaches: shapes with the same area but different perimeters, and the reverse
same_area.representation: shapes on squared paper; write area and perimeter for each; circle the pair that match

elapsed_stories.option: form "story": time-interval word problems with the time line as the drawing
elapsed_stories.name: Time Word Problems (option)
elapsed_stories.teaches: word problems adding and subtracting time intervals in minutes, drawn on a number-line (time line) diagram
elapsed_stories.representation: write the time or the minutes — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form
elapsed_stories.why: elapsed skills use time lines without stories

mass_scales.name: Read Scales (g, kg, ml, l)
mass_scales.teaches: reading mass and capacity scales in grams, kilograms, millilitres and litres with scale steps of 1, 2, 5, 10, 100
mass_scales.representation: a drawn dial or jug scale; write the reading with the unit; option: scale step
mass_scales.why: mass_volume_liquid reads scales on a few items, MC sort elsewhere

mass_ops.name: Mass and Capacity Word Problems
mass_ops.teaches: adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing masses and capacities in context
mass_ops.representation: picture of scales/jugs with values; write the answer with the unit

length_ops.name: Length Word Problems
length_ops.teaches: adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing lengths and heights in context (same units)
length_ops.representation: a drawn ruler or bar model with the lengths labelled; write the answer with its unit

money_2step.name: Two-Step Money Problems
money_2step.teaches: two-step money word problems (buy two items, then find the change)
money_2step.representation: a price list drawn as tags plus a short story; bar model support level

conversion_table.option: form "conversion table": complete a two-column table (1 ft = 12 in, 2 ft, 3 ft …) and use it
conversion_table.name: Conversion Tables (option)
conversion_table.teaches: knowing relative sizes of units in one system and recording equivalents in a two-column table (ft/in, m/cm, kg/g, lb/oz, l/ml, hr/min/sec)
conversion_table.representation: write the missing entries — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form

defining_attributes.name: Is It Still a Triangle?
defining_attributes.teaches: defining attributes (closed, number of straight sides, corners) versus non-defining attributes (colour-free: size, orientation, thickness of line)
defining_attributes.representation: tick yes / no; tick attributes from a bank — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form

map.taskType: is it still a triangle? (defining vs non-defining)

shapes_3d_props.name: 3-D Shapes: Names and Properties
shapes_3d_props.teaches: naming 3-D shapes (prisms, pyramids) from faces, edges and vertices and from their 2-D views or nets
shapes_3d_props.representation: a 3-D shape drawing with a property table; option: which net makes it

polygons.name: Regular and Irregular Polygons
polygons.teaches: naming polygons by the number of sides, and telling regular from irregular
polygons.representation: polygon line drawings; write the name and tick regular / irregular

hv_lines.name: Horizontal and Vertical Lines
hv_lines.teaches: recognising horizontal and vertical lines in shapes and on a grid
hv_lines.representation: shapes with sides marked; write H or V for each marked line

line_graph.name: Line Graphs
line_graph.teaches: reading and drawing line graphs that show change over time
line_graph.representation: a line graph on a grid with labelled axes; read values, find differences, or plot the points

table_data.name: Tables
table_data.teaches: reading and completing simple tables and tally-to-number tables
table_data.representation: a two-column table with blanks; fill in the counts; answer one question

four_quadrants.name: Coordinates in Four Quadrants (option)
four_quadrants.teaches: reading, plotting and solving problems with coordinates in four quadrants (missing vertices, midpoints)

measurable_attributes.name: What Can We Measure?
measurable_attributes.teaches: naming measurable attributes of one object (how long, how tall, how heavy, how much it holds) and telling measurable from not measurable (colour)
measurable_attributes.representation: tick words from a picture-word bank — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form

volume_fractional.option: fractional edge lengths (1/2 and 1/4 units) and packing with unit-fraction cubes
volume_fractional.name: Volume With Fractional Edges (option)
volume_fractional.teaches: volume of a prism with fractional edges by packing 1/2-unit cubes and by V = l × w × h = B × h
volume_fractional.representation: write the volume as a fraction or mixed number of cubic units — B&W boxed cell; screen keeps the production form

draw_angles.name: Draw Angles and Lines
draw_angles.teaches: drawing angles of a given size with a protractor and lines of a given length
draw_angles.representation: a protractor picture with a base line; the key shows the angle drawn; print-first skill

map.taskType: draw an angle of N degrees

reflect_grid.name: Reflect on a Grid
reflect_grid.teaches: reflecting a shape in a horizontal or vertical mirror line on a square grid and in the axes
reflect_grid.representation: a grid with a dashed mirror line and a shape; draw the reflection; key shows it
reflect_grid.why: geo_reflect is MC; reflect_grid gives the drawing form

map_heavier_lighter_bw.option: look "bw": B&W line-art objects (or a pan balance drawing) instead of emoji; answer is a label
map_heavier_lighter_bw.name: Heavier or Lighter, B&W pictures (option)
map_heavier_lighter_bw.teaches: comparing the mass of two objects by experience and on a pan balance
map_heavier_lighter_bw.representation: print: one boxed cell, two B&W outline objects labelled A and B (or a tipped balance), pupil circles or writes the letter; screen: click the object (production by selection of the object itself, two choices only)
map_heavier_lighter_bw.why: 200/200 answers are colour emoji, which breaks the B&W print contract; needs re-grade after the redraw

map_volume_expressions.option: form "expressions": pick every expression that gives the volume (l×w×h, B×h, layers added)
map_volume_expressions.name: Volume Expressions (option)
map_volume_expressions.teaches: that l×w×h, base area × height and repeated layers all give the volume
map_volume_expressions.representation: print: boxed cell with a B&W prism (edges labelled) and 4-5 expressions with check boxes, pupil ticks all that work; screen: multi-select check boxes (MAP's own form)
map_volume_expressions.why: MAP's top-band volume item; volume today only computes a number

map_shape_attribute_sort.name: Sort Shapes by Two Attributes
map_shape_attribute_sort.teaches: sorting figures by line of symmetry, angle type, or both
map_shape_attribute_sort.representation: print: boxed cell, 4-6 B&W figures lettered, a 3-column chart (A only / B only / both) where pupil writes letters; screen: drag letters/figures into chart columns
map_shape_attribute_sort.why: MAP 2-5 sample item; no skill sorts by two attributes

time_convert.name: Convert Units of Time (option)
time_convert.teaches: converting between seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years; MAP clause: small → large as h-and-min, decimal and mixed hours (90 min = 1 h 30 min = 1.5 h = 1 ½ h), and choose ALL measurements equal to a time
time_convert.representation: boxed cell with a 60-minute bar under the question, slots "__ h __ min" and "__ h"; choose-all form prints check boxes; screen: number entry (decimal or mixed accepted) and select-all-that-apply
time_convert.why: WRM time_convert (wrm.js) already plans the time option on unit_conversion_word; MAP adds the decimal/mixed-hours and choose-all clauses, so they join it instead of a duplicate

map_frac_side_area.option: form "area": a rectangle with fractional sides (e.g. 2/3 × 3/4 unit) drawn inside a unit square tiled by unit-fraction rectangles; count the tiles, then write the area as a product
map_frac_side_area.name: Area With Fractional Sides (option)
map_frac_side_area.teaches: finding the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling with unit-fraction squares and showing it equals the product of the sides
map_frac_side_area.representation: boxed cell, B&W unit square with the rectangle's tiles outlined (single grey shade), slots "__ tiles of 1/__ = __" and "__ × __ = __"; screen: fraction number entry, never multiple choice
map_frac_side_area.why: frac_mult_word deals garden-area stories (55/200 dist) and mult_frac_frac an overlap model with no area framing; neither tiles with unit-fraction squares, the clause 5.NF.B.4b names

turns_angles.name: Turns and Angles
turns_angles.teaches: an angle as an amount of turn; right angles as quarter turns; MAP clause: degrees as a fraction of 360 (a quarter turn = 90°, 1/360 of a turn = 1°)
turns_angles.representation: boxed cell with a circle and the turned ray, slots "__ turn = __°"; screen: number entry / click the turn, never MC where entry fits

map.taskType: angle as a turn of a circle

turns_angles.why: WRM turns_angles already planned (wrm.js); standards-audit gives 4.MD.C.5a/b a gap verdict
